tracks.publicName: Your dismissed North Carolina case may have cleared itself

controllingAuthority.summary: Where a person is charged with a misdemeanor, a felony or an infraction and all charges in the case are disposed on or after December 1, 2021 by dismissal, a finding of not guilty, or a finding of not responsible, the charges are expunged by operation of law not less than 180 and not more than 210 days after the date of final disposition, if the statutory conditions are met. The General Assembly postponed the automatic process until July 1, 2024; it is now underway.

exclusions: Dispositions before December 1, 2021.
Cases in which not every charge was disposed favorably.
Dismissals through deferred prosecution or conditional discharge, which are treated differently and route to the petition track.
Under G.S. 15A-146(a), no case with a felony charge dismissed pursuant to a plea agreement is expunged under that subsection.

Effective for dismissals on or after December 1, 2025, a dismissal by the court of a charge against a defendant found incapable to proceed is not eligible for expunction under G.S. 15A-146 and should not be included in an automatic expunction.

components.notes: Explains the December 1, 2021 disposition boundary, the July 1, 2024 start of the automatic process, the 180-to-210-day window measured from final disposition, the all-charges-disposed-favorably gate, the deferred prosecution and conditional discharge carve-out, the plea-agreement felony exclusion and the incapable-to-proceed exclusion; tells the participant to verify with an SBI criminal record check rather than assume; and states plainly that the court record clearing does not mean agency records cleared, because the clerk is not required to transmit the order.

controllingAuthority.summary: Where charges were expunged by operation of law under G.S. 15A-146(a4), the clerk is not required to transmit an expunction order to other entities. An agency that still holds and disseminates the charge may therefore be unaware the expunction occurred. G.S. 15A-153 restores the person to the status they occupied before the arrest, charge or conviction, and G.S. 15A-150 states the notification scheme for expunctions generally. This supporting action produces the participant's own written request asking the record holder to conform its records to the expunction that has already happened. It seeks no new relief and asks no court for anything.

exclusions: Any case where the automatic expunction under G.S. 15A-146(a4) has not in fact occurred. This action presupposes the expunction; where it did not run, the petition tracks apply instead.
Any case still inside the 180-to-210-day statutory window, which has not yet matured.
Federal record holders and out-of-state agencies, which North Carolina expunction does not reach.
The court record itself, which is the clerk's and the AOC's to maintain under G.S. 15A-151(a1).

destination.detail: Addressed to the agency the participant identifies from their own SBI criminal record check or from a background report. Nothing is filed with a court and no fee is paid. LegalEase writes the participant's request; it does not certify that the agency failed to act and does not assert that the expunction occurred as a matter of fact.

tracks.publicName: Clear a North Carolina charge that was dismissed

controllingAuthority.summary: On petition, the court expunges the records of a charge dismissed by the State or by the court, for a single dismissal under subsection (a) and for multiple dismissals under subsection (a1). There is no prior-conviction bar and no prior-expunction bar; the 2017 legislation eliminated the prior-expunction bar. A judge may grant the petition without a hearing under subsection (a6). Any petition under this section must be on a form approved by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

exclusions: No case with a felony charge dismissed pursuant to a plea agreement is expunged under subsection (a).

Effective for dismissals on or after December 1, 2025, a court dismissal of a charge against a defendant found incapable to proceed is not eligible. AOC-CR-287 (Dec. 2025) reflects this and does not limit the exclusion by date, which leaves earlier dismissals unresolved.
Out-of-state and federal convictions and charges are outside this relief; it reaches North Carolina records only.

tracks.publicName: Expunge a nonviolent North Carolina misdemeanor conviction

controllingAuthority.summary: On petition, the court may expunge nonviolent misdemeanor convictions. Nonviolent is defined by exclusion in G.S. 15A-145.5(a). The waiting period is three years for one nonviolent misdemeanor conviction, for petitions filed on or after July 9, 2025, and seven years for more than one, each measured from the conviction and completion of any active, probationary or post-release sentence, whichever is later. The petitioner consents to two record checks: the AOC checks for prior expunctions and the DPS State Bureau of Investigation checks for prior convictions. The district attorney is given notice and may be heard.

exclusions: Any Class A through G felony, so only Class H and I felonies can qualify as nonviolent.
Any Class A1 misdemeanor.
Impaired driving under G.S. 20-138.1 and related offenses. DWI is the classic trap.
Sex offenses and any offense requiring sex offender registration.
Offenses with assault as an essential element, certain offenses against minors, stalking and other enumerated crimes.
Methamphetamine offenses, certain controlled substance trafficking, and hate crimes, as enumerated.
Any non-traffic conviction at any time other than the offense or offenses being expunged bars relief on this track.
A new conviction during the waiting period.
Generally, more than one expunction under G.S. 15A-145.5 in a lifetime.
Outstanding restitution on the conviction to be expunged, until satisfied.
Pending charges at the time of the petition.
Out-of-state and federal convictions are not expungeable here, but they count toward eligibility.

controllingAuthority.summary: On petition, the court may expunge nonviolent felony convictions. Only Class H and I felonies can be nonviolent; Class A through G felonies are categorically out. The waiting period is ten years from completion of the sentence for one nonviolent felony conviction and twenty years for two or three. All nonviolent felonies disposed in the same session of court count as one nonviolent felony conviction for both the count and the waiting tier.

exclusions: Any Class A through G felony. Only Class H and I felonies can be nonviolent.
Sex offenses and any offense requiring sex offender registration.
Offenses with assault as an essential element, certain offenses against minors, stalking and other enumerated crimes.
Methamphetamine offenses, certain controlled substance trafficking, and hate crimes, as enumerated.
More than three nonviolent felony convictions.
Disqualifying convictions, and any new conviction during the waiting period.
Outstanding restitution on the conviction to be expunged, until satisfied.
Generally, more than one expunction under G.S. 15A-145.5 in a lifetime.
Pending charges at the time of the petition.
Out-of-state and federal convictions are not expungeable here, but they count toward eligibility.
